subject: Performance SLO + Load Test Coordination (FinWise)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO + Load Test Coordination (FinWise)

Hi Daniel / Anjali -

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and next steps so we have shared expectations for the customer-led load test: 

Recap of SLOs you shared:
- Latency: p50 < 150ms, p95 < 300ms for single-request generation (non-streaming).
- Streaming: initial-first-byte target < 100ms for streaming responses; token emission cadence ~50-100ms.
- Throughput/Concurrency: target sustained throughput ~200 req/s with peak concurrency ~50 concurrent requests.
- Payload: average request ~300 tokens; some large context queries up to 2k tokens.

What we need from your side to run the customer-led test (you mentioned you could run k6):
1) k6/Locust scripts (you said k6) + test scenario(s) - attach if possible.
2) IP ranges to whitelist on our side for the test runner(s).
3) Preferred test window(s) - you suggested Thu/Fri next week.
4) Which endpoints and model variants you want exercised (e.g., redwood/gpt-*-v1, streaming vs non-streaming).

Redwood actions:
- Provide a short-lived test API key and a test project/organization so your k6 runner hits a sandbox with realistic routing.
- Whitelist IP ranges you provide and lift any per-key rate limits for the duration of the test (we can set a protective cap to avoid noisy neighbor effects).
- Monitor during the test (latency, p50/p95, errors) and provide real-time logs if you want.

If you can send over the k6 scenario and IP list we'll get the test account prepared today.

Thanks - I'll loop in Aditya (SRE/solutions) and Rishi (AE support) to get the test account and allowlist aligned.

Best,
Marissa
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132

Attachments: (waiting on your k6 script)

Thanks Marissa - appreciate the clear recap. Attaching our initial k6 scenario and the IP ranges for our runners. A few notes from our side: 

- Script: finwise-k6-scenarios.js (attached). We have two scenarios:
  * steady-state (200 RPS for 30m)
  * ramp/peak (ramp from 10 RPS to 400 RPS over 15m, hold 10m, ramp down)
- IPs to whitelist (finwise-ip-allowlist.txt attached) - our CI runs from two runner pools in AWS us-west-2 and a corporate run from a static office IP.
- We want to exercise both streaming and non-streaming endpoints. For streaming tests, the script uses k6 + websocket client to simulate chunked responses.
- Preferred windows: Thu 2026-05-14 10:00-12:00 PDT or Fri 2026-05-15 09:00-11:00 PDT. We can confirm Thu if you can turn on the test key by EOD Wed.

Also listing the models we want to hit in order: redwood-compat/gpt-4o-instruct (non-stream), redwood-stream/gpt-4o-stream (streaming).

Let me know if you need the scripts adjusted - we can parameterize throughput or switch to Locust if needed.

Thanks,
Daniel
Senior Performance Engineer | FinWise
daniel.lee@finwise.com

Attachments: finwise-k6-scenarios.js, finwise-ip-allowlist.txt

Aditya / Rishi - forwarding FinWise's k6 script and IP list. Can you please: 

1) Create a short-lived test API key scoped to a sandbox project for FinWise (expiry 48h) and enable both streaming and non-streaming routes.

Also note the SLOs they listed (p95 <300ms, streaming first-byte <100ms). We'll monitor p50/p95 and error rates during the run and provide a post-test report.

If you want, we can run a short smoke at 10 RPS earlier on Thu to validate the workflow before the main ramp.

Thanks - cc'ing Daniel/Anjali for visibility.

Marissa
